intake.name: Linear integration (assign ticket, playbook label, @mention)
intake.summary: A Linear ticket can be assigned to Devin, tagged with a playbook label such as !plan, !implement, !triage or !review, or Devin can be @mentioned in a comment, each of which starts a session.

loop.name: Automations
loop.summary: Automations wire external events (Slack messages, GitHub webhooks, Linear ticket updates, schedules and custom webhooks) to Devin sessions that start automatically; a schedule trigger is either recurring (cron-based) or one-time.

execution.name: session
execution.summary: A Devin session comes with a Shell, an IDE (VSCode environment loaded with your repos) and a Browser that you can watch or take over, plus a read-only Side Chat for asking questions without interrupting the work.

demoable.summary: The Free self-serve plan lists limited Devin usage, plus access to Devin Review and DeepWiki.

execution.name: Droid (Missions, Exec Mode)
execution.summary: Droid CLI runs interactively in the terminal; multi-agent Missions are launched with /missions or droid exec --mission, scoped tasks can be delegated to Custom Droids via /droids, and Exec Mode (droid exec) runs headless in scripts and CI/CD.

intake.name: Copilot cloud agent
intake.summary: Work can be started from the agents panel, a conversation, or an issue or pull request on GitHub.com; code scanning alerts from security campaigns can also be assigned to it.

loop.name: Automations
loop.summary: Automations let you define a task once and have Copilot cloud agent run it on a schedule or in response to repository events.

planning.omitted: No first-party planning page verified; the about page only mentions asking an agent to plan in chat.

execution.name: Copilot cloud agent
execution.summary: It works in an ephemeral cloud development environment rather than your local IDE, where it can edit files and run tests and linters.

intake.name: conversation
intake.summary: In OpenHands Cloud's Slack app, a new conversation starts by mentioning @openhands in a new message or a thread in any Slack channel.

loop.name: Automations
loop.summary: Automations schedule AI-powered tasks that run automatically on a cron schedule (for example every Monday at 9 AM); each run gets a fresh sandbox.

execution.name: sandbox
execution.summary: A sandbox is the environment where OpenHands runs commands, edits files and starts servers; providers are Docker (recommended), Process (unsafe but fast) and Remote.

demoable.summary: The GitHub repository states an MIT license and says agents can be run locally, in Docker, on VMs, or anywhere an agent server backend runs.

intake.name: Cloud agents
intake.summary: Cloud agents can be started from Cursor for iOS, Cursor Web, Cursor Desktop, Slack via @cursor, @cursor comments on GitHub or Bitbucket PRs, Linear, or the API.

loop.name: Automations (triggers)
loop.summary: Automations run cloud agents in the background, either on a schedule (preset or cron expression) or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Linear and more; a webhook trigger gives a private HTTP endpoint that starts a run when posted to.

planning.name: Plan Mode
planning.summary: Plan Mode has the agent ask clarifying questions, research the codebase and produce an implementation plan you can review and edit before any code is written.

execution.name: Cloud agents
execution.summary: Cloud agents run in isolated VMs in the cloud with full development environments (cloned repos, installed dependencies, secrets, startup commands, network access).

demoable.summary: The docs say Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and are charged at API pricing for the selected model.

intake.name: code agents
intake.summary: Per the overview, work can be started through the Slack integration, the Linear integration, or programmatically with the Python SDK/API.

execution.name: code agents
execution.summary: The overview says agents can safely run code, install dependencies and test changes in isolated environments, and can create branches, commit code and review PRs.

intake.name: surfaces
intake.summary: Claude Code runs from the terminal, IDE extensions, a desktop app and the web; a bug report can also be routed from Slack by mentioning @Claude to get a pull request back, and GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD can automate PR review and issue triage.

loop.name: Routines
loop.summary: A routine is a saved Claude Code configuration that runs automatically on a schedule (recurring or one-off), from an HTTP POST to its API endpoint, or in response to GitHub events, on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure.

planning.name: plan mode
planning.summary: In plan mode Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve; start it with --permission-mode plan or Shift+Tab.

execution.name: session
execution.summary: Claude Code reads the codebase, edits files and runs commands in a session; subagents and background agents can run work in parallel, and claude -p runs non-interactively for CI.

destination.summary: The overview points to parallel subagents, background agents, scheduled Routines and the Agent SDK for custom orchestration.
